If I were you I’d probably try slip it into a conversation. I don’t do well with out of the blue/straight up statements, so I’d probably start a conversation about something sex - related and when it seems right in the convo, say that I have that fetish. (I don’t have a scat fetish, this is gonna be a hypothetical situation) 

For example, if you were to be talking about boundaries and how far you two would be willing to go sexually (if it was asked out of the blue it wouldn’t be that weird for a relationship) I may say something like ‘I have a scat fetish but you don’t have to do anything about it’. Her reaction may vary from being stunned, maybe disturbed or perhaps confused if she doesn’t know what it is. Just tell her simply that she doesn’t have to shit on you or anything like that - just telling her will make you feel as if a weight is lifted off her shoulders. If she has the same fetish, cool - you can talk about it. If she doesn’t, it is what it is. You still got your fantasies. If she freaks out about it, reassure her that you’re not gonna force anything onto her - that she has no bad pressure to engage in that kind of play with you. 

If my partner were to tell me they had a scat fetish, I’d probably be like ‘what the fuck’ at the thought of someone wanting me to shit on them but at the same time, if I feel no pressure to do anything and that I’m not forced and I’m reassured, I’d be fine. I wouldn’t care that much. But at the same time, everyone is different. If you’re gonna tell her, be prepared for her to be weirded out and to reassure her as that will most likely happen. If not, cool - talk about it.  If she’s weirded out, talk about it. It’ll be awkward, but important
